name: evidence-v1
goal: Each story gives concrete, observable evidence for at least one world condition
problem: Rewrite abstract conditions (prices, energy, trust, division, health) as concrete evidence atoms and test whether Clef agrees with itself
note: Each atom is asked twice in different words (a, b) plus once reversed. Self-agreement a vs b says whether the atom is learnable. Written before any answers were seen.

probes.a: Does {file} report a price that consumers pay going up, such as food, rent, fares or household bills?
probes.b: Does {file} say that shoppers, tenants or households now pay more for something than before?
probes.reversed: Does {file} report a price that consumers pay going down?

probes.a: Does {file} report an inflation rate, a tariff or a tax going up?
probes.b: Does {file} give a number showing inflation, a tariff or a tax getting higher?
probes.reversed: Does {file} report an inflation rate, a tariff or a tax going down?

probes.a: Does {file} report fuel, gas or electricity prices going up?
probes.b: Does {file} say petrol, gas or power bills are getting more expensive?
probes.reversed: Does {file} report fuel, gas or electricity prices going down?

probes.a: Does {file} report an energy supply cut, fuel shortage, blackout or attack on an energy site?
probes.b: Does {file} describe fuel or power not reaching people, or a power plant, pipeline or refinery being shut or damaged?
probes.reversed: Does {file} report energy supply being restored or increased?

probes.a: Does {file} report a government body, court, police force or public official accused of wrongdoing or a cover-up?
probes.b: Does {file} describe officials or a public institution facing a scandal, inquiry or misconduct claims?
probes.reversed: Does {file} report a public official or institution being cleared of wrongdoing?

probes.a: Does {file} report people saying they no longer trust a government, court, police force or official?
probes.b: Does {file} cite a poll, protest or public statement showing falling confidence in a public institution?
probes.reversed: Does {file} report confidence in a public institution rising?

probes.a: Does {file} report open hostility, clashes or hate between ethnic, religious or social groups?
probes.b: Does {file} describe one community or group of people attacking, abusing or rallying against another?
probes.reversed: Does {file} report two groups or communities reconciling or working together?

probes.a: Does {file} report political parties or voters becoming more bitterly split?
probes.b: Does {file} describe a deep, angry divide between political camps or their supporters?
probes.reversed: Does {file} report rival political camps agreeing or cooperating?

probes.a: Does {file} report people falling ill, being injured or dying from a disease, accident, disaster or harmful product?
probes.b: Does {file} describe illness, injuries or deaths affecting people?
probes.reversed: Does {file} report people recovering, or a health threat being brought under control?

decisions: Where does the story in {file} mainly take place or matter?
How much does the story in {file} change ordinary people's lives?
Can this be answered from the story text shown?
